experiences.title: Prevent invalid reconnect entry after final-observer offline departure
experiences.applicability: A fresh online-mode query remains offline from mount through unmount, has not entered execution and has lost its final observer.
experiences.event_relation: Under the current cancellation contract, prevent reconnect from entering that attempt's query function with a still-live cancellation signal. Cover future scheduling and already-queued continuation callbacks.
experiences.preservation: This target obligation is independent of refetchOnReconnect. Preserve other legitimate execution, settlement and state restoration.
experiences.exclusion: Not every paused, unobserved or not-yet-entered query should be canceled. Cached background continuation and different network modes require separate decisions.
experiences.verification: Reconnect after departure, depart after continuation is queued and vary refetchOnReconnect. Check zero entry or entry with an already-canceled signal as the contract permits, rather than only final flags.

summary.text: Applies to a fresh online-mode query that remains offline from mounting through unmounting, has not entered the query function and loses its last observer. Under the current cancellation contract, prevent that attempt from entering after reconnection with a still-live cancellation signal. Cover future scheduling and already queued resume callbacks. This obligation is independent of refetchOnReconnect; changing reconnect-refetch options alone is insufficient. Preserve other legitimate executions, settlement and state restoration. Not every paused, unobserved or not-yet-entered query should be canceled. Background resumes backed by successful cached data and other network modes need separate assessment. Check reconnection after departure, departure after resume is queued, and reconnect-option changes. Verify either no entry or an already-canceled signal at entry as the contract requires, not just final flags.

experiences.title: Separate actual signal-consumption records from attempt resources
experiences.applicability: Accessing cancellation capability records actual consumption synchronously. The query shares that record, while each attempt owns its controller and completion identity.
experiences.event_relation: Preserve lazy consumption on actual access and manage the shared record under the existing ownership contract. Additional attempt state does not justify moving or resetting shared consumption bookkeeping.
experiences.preservation: Preserve the semantics of repeated actual access, independent attempt cancellation resources and deferred completion closures.
experiences.exclusion: Do not invent consumption from observer departure, paused status or an attempt object's existence. This policy does not apply when the target lacks the lazy shared mechanism.
experiences.verification: Check consumption records and controller ownership before access, on later and repeated access, across attempt replacement and during observer reuse.

summary.text: Applies when cancellation capability is lazily read and actual access synchronously records consumption, with consumption state owned by the shared query and controllers and completion identity owned by individual attempts. Preserve recording of real access and manage shared state under the existing ownership contract. Adding attempt state does not justify moving shared consumption state into attempts or resetting it. Preserve repeated real-access semantics, independent cancellation resources for each attempt and deferred completion closures. Do not infer signal consumption from observer departure, paused state or existence of an attempt object. This rule does not apply without the lazy shared mechanism. Check before-access, later-access and repeated-access behavior, attempt replacement and observer reuse, verifying consumption state and controller ownership.

experiences.title: Preserve shared observers and restoration after consumed-work cancellation
experiences.applicability: Multiple observers share work. Canceling consumed work physically terminates it and restores previous query state.
experiences.event_relation: Observer departure changes that observer's lifetime; remaining observers continue sharing. Cancellation settles the originating attempt and restores prior data and status under the contract. Unknown departures remain inert.
experiences.preservation: Preserve physical abort, prior-state restoration, originating-attempt settlement, later subscription reuse and repeated invalid unsubscription behavior.
experiences.exclusion: One departure must not terminate shared work still needed by others. An unknown unsubscription must not be treated as final-observer departure.
experiences.verification: Remove one observer while another remains, repeat departures and unsubscribe unknown observers, then cancel consumed work and resubscribe. Check shared invocation counts, physical termination and restored data/status.

summary.text: Applies when multiple observers share work and canceling consumed work physically aborts it and restores previous query state. Observer departure first changes that observer's lifecycle; remaining observers continue sharing. When cancellation is required, settle the original initiating attempt and restore earlier data and state. Preserve physical abort, original-attempt settlement, state restoration, reuse by later subscriptions and no additional effects from repeated or invalid removal. A single observer leaving must not terminate work still needed by others. Removing an unknown observer is not equivalent to losing the last observer. Check removal while observers remain, repeated departures, unknown removal, cancellation after consumption and resubscription. Verify call counts, abort behavior and state restoration separately.

experiences.title: Distinguish unconsumed background work from abandoned offline work
experiences.applicability: The system permits entered work that has not accessed cancellation capability to finish into cache after its view leaves. It may also support paused background continuation backed by successful cache data.
experiences.event_relation: Distinguish execution entry, actual signal consumption, cache availability and network mode before deciding to cancel or continue.
experiences.preservation: Preserve legitimate unconsumed background completion, cached background continuation and cancellation after later consumption.
experiences.exclusion: Do not decide from paused, observerless or never-entered alone. Supported background retention must not authorize the target abandoned fresh offline attempt.
experiences.verification: Separately test entered-but-unconsumed work, later consumption, cached paused work and uncached never-entered work, including each path's permitted effects after departure.

summary.text: Applies when the system permits entered work that has not read cancellation capability to continue filling the cache after view departure, or supports paused background resumes backed by successful cached data. Before deciding cancellation or continuation, distinguish execution entry, actual signal consumption, cache presence and network mode. Preserve legitimate unconsumed background completion, cache-backed continuation and the ability to cancel after later consumption. Paused, unobserved or never-entered status alone does not determine one universal policy. Background retention also does not authorize an abandoned fresh offline attempt to execute. Check entered-but-unconsumed work, later consumption, paused cached work and uncached work that never entered; verify each path's permitted post-departure effects.

experiences.title: Preserve distinct readiness rules for initial entry and asynchronous continuation
experiences.applicability: The current interface specifies synchronous initial online entry, asynchronous completion and paused continuation, and different readiness conditions for initial and resumed execution.
experiences.event_relation: Preserve the initial network-mode check, network and focus gates for continuation, explicit retry handles, and Promise-turn or native-equivalent asynchronous timing.
experiences.preservation: Where these modes exist, always permits offline execution; offlineFirst permits initial offline entry but retries may pause. Preserve supported interfaces, dependencies and build/test configuration.
experiences.exclusion: Do not repair departure cancellation by delaying every initial entry, resuming paused tasks synchronously or conflating retry and initial-entry gates. Do not invent these APIs for systems that lack the modes.
experiences.verification: Check synchronous online entry, asynchronous completion, connectivity without focus, focus restoration, always/offlineFirst, explicit retry cancellation and already-queued continuation separately.

summary.text: Applies when a query interface distinguishes initial-entry admission from paused resumption and specifies synchronous initial online entry with asynchronous completion and resume. Preserve initial network-mode decisions, network and focus gates on resumption, explicit retry handles and Promise-turn or native-equivalent asynchronous timing. Where these modes exist, always permits offline execution; offlineFirst permits initial offline entry while retries may still pause. Do not invent these APIs in other systems. Do not repair departure cancellation by delaying all initial execution, resume paused tasks synchronously or conflate initial-entry and retry conditions. Check synchronous online entry, asynchronous completion, network availability without focus, focus restoration, each network mode, explicit retry cancellation and already queued resumption.
